cards.text: Chronicles has been tracing Israel's family tree tribe by tribe (1 Chronicles 2–5), and now it's Levi's turn, starting with his sons Gershon, Kohath and Merari. From Kohath's son Amram come Aaron, whom God set apart to serve as priest (Exodus 28:1), Moses, Israel's leader, and their sister Miriam the prophetess (Exodus 15:20). One house gave Israel a priest, a leader AND a prophetess, and I can't get one batch out of the oven without burning a corner.

From Aaron's son Eleazar, the line of priests runs father to son, through names like Phinehas and Zadok, and an Azariah who served as priest in the temple Solomon built in Jerusalem. It ends with Jehozadak, who went into captivity when the LORD sent Judah and Jerusalem into exile by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon (2 Kings 25:1).

Then comes the clan list: Gershom, Kohath and Merari, each with his family down the line. There's an Elkanah, then another Elkanah, then ANOTHER Elkanah. Friend, if you yell 'Elkanah!' in this family, you'd better say which one. And then come the sons of Samuel, the prophet who anointed David (1 Samuel 16:13): Joel and Abijah.
Then the list pauses for a job description: these are the men King David put in charge of the music in the house of the LORD. FINALLY, a list where somebody gets a microphone!

cards.question: When does David put these men in charge of the music in the house of the LORD?

answers.text: After the city walls were rebuilt

cards.question: David's music men ministered with ___ before the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting, until Solomon built the house of the LORD in Jerusalem.
True or false: David's singers worked out their own way of serving as they went along.

cards.text: Now we meet the men who served, together with their sons, starting with Heman the singer from the Kohathites. His line climbs back through Samuel, Korah and Kohath all the way to Levi, the son of Israel. That's a LOT of 'son of.' Me? My whole family history is a bakery bin and a 25-cent sticker.

cards.question: Heman the singer has a kinsman who serves at his right hand. Who is it?

cards.text: Asaph's line runs back through Shimei and Jahath to Gershom, the son of Levi. So Heman is Kohath's guy, and Asaph is Gershom's guy.

cards.question: Heman the singer is from Kohath's clan, and Asaph at his right hand is from Gershom's. Which kinsmen stand on the left?

cards.text: Named for the left side is Ethan, the son of Kishi, whose line runs back through Mahli and Mushi to Merari, the son of Levi. Three clans, one choir. I sang to my oven once, friend. The timer went off EARLY. Just to drown me out.
Back to the rest of the tribe. Their fellow Levites are assigned to serve at the tabernacle, the house of God.

cards.question: True or false: These fellow Levites stick to just one kind of service at the tabernacle.
The Levites handle every kind of service at the tabernacle, but all the work of the Most Holy Place is done by ___ and his sons.
Aaron and his sons present offerings on the altar of burnt offering and on the altar of incense. What are the offerings for?

answers.text: To ask for rain on the land

cards.question: Aaron and his sons did their work according to all that ___ the servant of God had commanded.

cards.text: Aaron's line comes back for a quick encore, down to Zadok and his son Ahimaaz. Then the Levites are given cities with pasturelands, assigned by lot, and the first lot falls to Aaron's descendants. Their list starts with Hebron, a city of refuge, though the fields and villages around it go to Caleb son of Jephunneh, one of the men Moses sent to scout the land (Numbers 13:3, 6). From there, every Levite clan gets towns from tribes on both sides of the Jordan, and Shechem in Ephraim's hill country is a city of refuge too. Take it from a guy who lived years in the back of a junk drawer: a place to call home is a BIG deal.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 1 has a dash outside a quotation: "Chronicles has been tracing Israel's family tree tribe by tribe (1 Chronicles 2–5), and now it's Levi's turn, starting with his sons Gershon, Kohath and Merari. From Kohath's son Amram come Aaron, whom God set apart to serve as priest (Exodus 28:1), Moses, Israel's leader, and their sister Miriam the prophetess (Exodus 15:20). One house gave Israel a priest, a leader AND a prophetess, and I can't get one batch out of the oven without burning a corner."

rule.text: No em dashes or en dashes to make a sentence longer.

findings.problem: Solomon shows up here for the first time ("the temple Solomon built in Jerusalem"), but the card never says who he is, for example David's son, king of Israel.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: David shows up here for the first time ("the prophet who anointed David"), but the card never says who he is. He is only identified as King David on card 4.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The blank's answer, "song," is given away twice. Card 4 already says David put these men "in charge of the music," and the question itself calls them "David's music men." Next to that, "incense" and "offerings" are easy to rule out. Card 4 is a story card, not an answered choice, so the follow-up exception doesn't apply.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later. Once a choice has been answered, the cards after it can build on that answer. ... A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The singers' genealogy (1 Chronicles 6:33-47) is a long stretch of "son of" lists. It is split across three story cards (8, 10, 12) instead of being summed up in one. Cards 8 and 12 also run 4 sentences each, which is only allowed for a single summary card. The right hand and left hand placement of Heman, Asaph and Ethan could be the standout detail on that one card.

rule.text: Papa Dorin sums up the stretch in one story card. A short story inside the stretch, like Nimrod in the list of nations (Genesis 10:8–12), is part of the stretch: it can be the standout detail on that card, but it gets no choice cards.

findings.problem: This choice card asks about a name inside the singers' genealogy (Asaph, 6:39), which is part of a long stretch. It is also a pure discovery question.

rule.text: A long stretch never gets a choice card.

findings.problem: This choice card asks about a detail inside the singers' genealogy (the sons of Merari on the left, 6:44), which is part of a long stretch.

rule.text: A long stretch never gets a choice card.

findings.problem: "These fellow Levites" points back to card 13, which is no longer on screen. The question doesn't say whose fellow Levites they are, or that they are the Levites other than the singers.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: "Every Levite clan gets towns from tribes on both sides of the Jordan" reads as if each clan got towns on both sides. The Kohathites got cities only from Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim and the half-tribe of Manasseh (6:57-60, 66-70), all west of the Jordan. Only the Gershomites and the Merarites got towns on both sides.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.
